cells.tense: You are tending what is still alive in the middle of an ending, and your hand is steady.
cells.ask: Let one finished thing be finished today — mark what it gave you and set it down.
cells.core:
You are choosing what still deserves your care while something else closes, and you are doing it cleanly. The care isn't frantic and it isn't absent. You tend what remains, you let the rest go, and you keep both hands on the same thing at once. This is what tending looks like in a clearing: nothing ripped out, nothing left to rot in place.

What finishes now finishes at your pace, and it takes its place in what comes next. The ending stops being a debt and becomes ground you walk on. That is the reward of doing this part well — you get to keep moving, and what you tended keeps growing behind you.
cells.sheetLine: You tend what's still alive while an ending runs, and you don't force it.
cells.verb: Tending what's growing with steady, responsible care
cells.place: The clearing where what must end for the new to begin

cells.tense: You're already at the far side of this ending, living out a clearing that hasn't happened yet.
cells.ask: Name one thing still here that is finished, and shelve the day you're rehearsing.
cells.core:
Tending here is simple when it's working: you see what's growing, you give it what it needs, and you let the finished thing go at the pace it actually goes. Your hands stay open, the clearing runs, and the next thing arrives on its own schedule.

But you are caring for what is growing before the old thing has ended, so your hands are full. Every decision gets made ahead of the moment it belongs to. You hold two loads at once by taking both on now, and the grip tightens until the care wears you out. There is a clearing waiting for you today. Name what is finished and mean it. The new thing can wait until it is actually in front of you, and it will be sturdier for being tended when it arrives. You get your hands back, and they stop doing tomorrow's work.
cells.sheetLine: You're caring ahead of the moment and tightening the grip.
cells.verb: Tending what's growing with steady, responsible care
cells.place: The clearing where what must end for the new to begin

cells.tense: You stopped tending, and you are still standing where you stopped.
cells.ask: Say the old thing out loud to one person once, then guard what's still alive.
cells.core:
Tending, when it is running here, looks like this: you look at a room or a habit or a person and you give it exactly what it needs, no more. You end what needs ending without ceremony, you keep the living things watered, and you do not carry the finished ones around with you. The clearing stays clear.

What stopped is the tending, and the clearing did not run. The endings sit there untended, and the living things are waiting for the attention that used to show up. Hope is what carries you through this. Tell someone the whole hope once — the one you have been keeping quiet because saying it felt like too much — and let that be the first small thing you tend. End the finished thing. The care comes back with it.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped tending and the clearing never ran.
cells.verb: Tending what's growing with steady, responsible care
cells.place: The clearing where what must end for the new to begin

cells.tense: You're clearing ground already, and you call it something the day is doing to you.
cells.ask: Own aloud one ending you chose — the ground under a thing that grew back.
cells.core:
Tending here, at its plainest, is choosing what stays and giving it steady care while the rest is allowed to end. It has no drama in it. The finished thing goes, the living thing gets fed, and the person doing it knows they are the one doing it.

That last part is where this is running without you. You leave jobs, rooms, habits, and it moves you forward — and the account is filed as the calendar's work or someone else's decision. You let the thing end. You just have not stood in front of it and said you chose it. Say one ending is yours, and notice what can grow in that clearing. The saying is the tending; without it the care has no author.
cells.sheetLine: You're already clearing the ground. The choosing is yours and unclaimed.
